items.title: 1.10 Solving Problems Involving Exponential and Logarithmic Equations and Inequalities (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Book p. 24-28: 1.10 intro, equations (Examples 15, 16, 16 again, 17), inequations (Examples 19, 20, 21); Example 16 printed twice, no Example 18

blocks.text: Assalam-o-alaikum bachon! Aaj ka sabaq is unit ka bohat kaam ka hissa hai. Ab tak aap ne exponential function \(a^x\) aur logarithmic function \(\log_a x\) ke graphs aur properties parhi hain. Aaj hum in hi properties ko istemal kar ke aisi equations aur inequalities hal karenge jin mein unknown \(x\) ya to power (exponent) mein chhupa hua hai, ya logarithm ke andar band hai. Misaal ke taur par \(4^{x-1} = 8\) mein \(x\) power mein hai, aur \(\log x + \log(x - 3) = 1\) mein \(x\) logarithm ke andar hai. Aam algebra ke tareeqe (jama, tafreeq, cross multiply) yahan seedhe kaam nahi karte, is liye humein naye auzaar (tools) chahiye.

Kitab kehti hai: is hisse mein hum aisi exponential aur logarithmic equations aur inequalities hal karte hain jin mein variable exponent mein ya logarithmic expression ke andar hota hai. Hal karne se pehle domain (woh values jin par expression maujood ho) ko zaroor dekhna hai, khaas taur par jab expression har real value par defined na ho. Tareeqe neeche di gayi misaalon se samjhaye gaye hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Is poore sabaq mein sirf chaar auzaar (tools) baar baar kaam aayenge. Inhein achhi tarah pehchaan lein:
1. Pehle domain: \(\log_a u\) sirf tab maujood hai jab \(u > 0\) ho (aur base \(a > 0,\ a \ne 1\)). Jab ke \(a^u\) har real \(u\) ke liye maujood hai aur hamesha positive hota hai. Domain ko ghar ki chaar diwari samjhein: jawab is ke andar hi hona chahiye.
2. One-to-one property (aik se aik rishta): \(a^u = a^v \iff u = v\) aur \(\log_a u = \log_a v \iff u = v\). Yani base ek jaisa ho to powers ya arguments barabar rakh sakte hain.
3. Laws of logarithms (product, quotient, power): kai logarithms ko jor kar ek bana dete hain, aur power ko neeche utaar dete hain.
4. Shakal badalna: \(\log_a u = k \iff u = a^k\). Log wali equation ko exponential shakal mein badalne se aksar seedhi algebra wali equation ban jati hai.
Aakhir mein har jawab ko domain se zaroor milana hai; jo value domain se bahar ho, woh rad (reject) hogi.
Examples of Exponential and Logarithmic Equations
Pehle equations dekhte hain. Har misaal mein hum ek hi tarteeb rakhenge: diya kya hai, domain kya hai, kaunsa auzaar lagega, phir hal, aur aakhir mein tasdeeq (check).

blocks.title: Example 15
steps:
Diya gaya: \(4^{x-1} = 8\).
Maloom karna: woh tamam real \(x\) jo is equation ko poora karein.
Tareeqa: dono taraf ek hi base (2) ki powers bana denge, phir one-to-one property se powers barabar rakh denge. Yeh tareeqa tab sab se aasan hai jab dono numbers ek hi base ki powers hon, jaise 4 aur 8 dono 2 ki powers hain.

Domain
\[\text{Domain} = ]-\infty, \infty[\]
Kyun: \(4^{x-1}\) har real number ke liye maujood hai, kyunke positive base ki koi bhi power li ja sakti hai. Is liye koi value nikalni nahi padti.

Dono taraf base 2 banayein
\[4 = 2^2,\quad 8 = 2^3\]
\[(2^2)^{x-1} = 2^3\]
\[2^{2x-2} = 2^3\]
Kyun: 4 aur 8 dono 2 ki powers hain. Rule \((a^m)^n = a^{mn}\) se \(2^{2(x-1)} = 2^{2x-2}\) bana. Dhyan dein: 2 ko poori bracket \((x - 1)\) se multiply karna hai, sirf \(x\) se nahi.

Powers barabar rakhein
\[2x - 2 = 3\]
\[x = \dfrac{5}{2}\]
Kyun: exponential function one-to-one hai: agar ek hi base ki do powers barabar hon to un ke exponents bhi barabar hone chahiye. Phir seedhi linear equation: \(2x = 5\).

Tasdeeq:
\[4^{\frac{5}{2} - 1} = 4^{\frac{3}{2}}\]
\[= (\sqrt{4})^3 = 2^3 = 8 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: \(4^{\frac{3}{2}}\) ka matlab hai pehle square root (2), phir cube (8). Jawab bilkul sahi hai.

blocks.text: Lekin har dafa itni aasani nahi hoti. Neeche wale chhote sawal ke baad jo misaal aati hai, us mein ek taraf 2 ki power hai aur doosri taraf 3 ki power. 2 aur 3 ko kisi bhi tarah ek hi base ki powers nahi banaya ja sakta. Aisi soorat mein hum ek aur auzaar uthate hain: dono taraf logarithm le lete hain. Logarithm ka power law is kaam ke liye bana hai ke woh power ko utha kar aage multiply ki jagah le aata hai. Jaise hi \(x\) power se neeche aaya, sawal ek aam linear equation ban jata hai jo aap pichli classon se hal karte aa rahe hain.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Isi tareeqe se \(9^x = 27\) hal kar ke dekhiye. Ishara: 9 aur 27 dono 3 ki powers hain. (Jawab: \(3^{2x} = 3^3\), is liye \(x = \frac{3}{2}\).)

blocks.title: Example 16
steps:
Diya gaya: \(2^{2x} - 3^{5x+3} = 0\).
Maloom karna: real solution \(x\).
Tareeqa: yahan base 2 aur 3 hain, jinhein ek jaisa nahi banaya ja sakta. Aisi soorat mein dono taraf natural logarithm (\(\ln\)) lete hain. Power law power ko neeche utaar deta hai aur equation \(x\) mein seedhi linear ban jati hai.

Equation ko dobara likhein aur domain dekhein
\[2^{2x} = 3^{5x+3} \quad \text{...(1)}\]
\[\text{Domain} = ]-\infty, \infty[\]
Kyun: ek term ko doosri taraf le jane se do powers barabar ho gayin. \(2^{2x}\) aur \(3^{5x+3}\) dono har real number ke liye maujood hain.

Equation (1) ke dono taraf natural logarithm lein
\[\ln 2^{2x} = \ln 3^{5x+3}\]
Kyun: dono taraf positive numbers hain, is liye un ka logarithm maujood hai; aur barabar numbers ke logarithm bhi barabar hote hain. Yeh bilkul aisa hai jaise dono taraf ek hi kaam (square, ya 2 se multiply) kar dena.

Power law lagayein
\[2x\ln 2 = (5x + 3)\ln 3\]
\[2x\ln 2 = 5x\ln 3 + 3\ln 3\]
Kyun: \(\ln a^k = k\ln a\). Ab \(x\) power se neeche aa gaya, yahi is tareeqe ka asal faida hai. Dhyan dein: \((5x + 3)\) poori bracket \(\ln 3\) se multiply hogi.

\(x\) wali terms ek taraf jama karein
\[(2\ln 2 - 5\ln 3)x = 3\ln 3\]
Kyun: ab yeh aam linear equation hai: \(x\) wali terms ek taraf, baaki doosri taraf, aur \(x\) ko common nikal liya. Yaad rakhiye \(\ln 2\) aur \(\ln 3\) sirf numbers hain (lagbhag 0.693 aur 1.099).

Power law, phir quotient law
\[(\ln 2^2 - \ln 3^5)x = \ln 3^3\]
\[(\ln 4 - \ln 243)x = \ln 27\]
\[x\ln\left(\dfrac{4}{243}\right) = \ln 27\]
Kyun: \(k\ln a = \ln a^k\) ulti taraf se parha, phir \(\ln m - \ln n = \ln\frac{m}{n}\). Is se jawab chhota aur saaf ho jata hai.

\(x\) nikalein
\[x = \dfrac{\ln 27}{\ln\left(\frac{4}{243}\right)}\]
\[x = \log_{\frac{4}{243}}(27)\]
Kyun: \(\ln\frac{4}{243}\) se divide kiya; yeh zero nahi kyunke \(\frac{4}{243} \ne 1\). Change of base formula \(\log_b a = \frac{\ln a}{\ln b}\) is fraction ko ek hi logarithm bana deta hai.

Tasdeeq:
\[x \approx \dfrac{3.2958}{-4.1068} \approx -0.8025\]
\[2^{2x} \approx 0.3287\]
\[3^{5x+3} \approx 0.3287 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: calculator se dono taraf ki values barabar aati hain, is liye jawab sahi hai. Jawab negative hai, aur yeh bilkul theek hai: domain mein har real number shamil tha.

blocks.title: Example 16
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\log x + \log(x - 3) = 1\) (yahan \(\log\) ka matlab base 10 hai).
Maloom karna: real solutions \(x\).
Tareeqa: pehle domain, phir product law se dono logarithms ko ek banayenge, phir exponential shakal, phir quadratic hal kar ke jo root domain se bahar ho usay rad karenge.

Domain
\[x > 0 \text{ and } x - 3 > 0\]
\[\Rightarrow x > 3\]
\[\text{Domain} = ]3, \infty[\]
Kyun: logarithm sirf positive argument ka hota hai. Dono shartein ek saath poori honi chahiyen; \(x > 3\) ho to \(x > 0\) khud ba khud ho jata hai.

Left side par product law
\[\log[x(x - 3)] = 1\]
Kyun: \(\log m + \log n = \log(mn)\). Do logs ka jama ek log ban gaya.

Exponential shakal mein likhein
\[x(x - 3) = 10^1 = 10\]
Kyun: \(\log_{10} u = k \iff u = 10^k\). Ab log khatam aur seedhi algebra shuru.

Factorize karein
\[x^2 - 3x - 10 = 0\]
\[(x - 5)(x + 2) = 0\]
\[x = 5 \text{ or } x = -2\]
Kyun: aise do numbers chahiye jin ka product \(-10\) aur jama \(-3\) ho: \(-5\) aur \(+2\).

Domain se milayein
\(5 \in ]3, \infty[\): qabool. \(-2 \notin ]3, \infty[\): rad.
Kyun: \(x = -2\) par \(\log(-2)\) maujood hi nahi. Product law ne logs ko jor diya tha, aur isi qadam ne ek faltu (extraneous) root andar aane diya. Isi liye domain check zaroori hai.

Tasdeeq:
\[\log 5 + \log(5 - 3)\]
\[= \log 5 + \log 2 = \log 10 = 1 \;\checkmark\]

blocks.title: Numbering note (ours)
blocks.text: Kitab mein "Example 16" ka number do dafa chhapa hai: pehli dafa \(2^{2x} - 3^{5x+3} = 0\) ke liye, doosri dafa \(\log x + \log(x - 3) = 1\) ke liye. Aur Example 17 ke baad seedha Example 19 aata hai; Example 18 kitab mein hai hi nahi. Hum ne chhape hue number hi rakhe hain taa ke aap har misaal kitab mein aasani se dhoondh sakein.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Doosri Example 16 se ek bohat ahem sabaq milta hai. Jab hum \(\log x + \log(x - 3)\) ko jor kar \(\log[x(x - 3)]\) likhte hain to naya expression \(x = -2\) par bhi maujood hai, kyunke \((-2)(-5) = 10\) positive hai. Lekin asal sawal mein \(\log(-2)\) aur \(\log(-5)\) maujood hi nahi. Yani laws lagane se domain chupke se bara ho jata hai aur faltu (extraneous) roots andar aa jati hain. Is ka ilaaj sirf ek hai: domain hamesha asal sawal se nikalein, aur aakhir mein har root ko us se milayein.

Ab ek dilchasp sawal dekhte hain jis mein \(x\) sirf argument mein nahi, balke logarithm ke base mein bhi baitha hai. Aise sawal mein do qisam ki shartein lagti hain: base ki shart aur argument ki shart. Ghabraiye mat, tareeqa wohi rahega: shartein likho, exponential shakal mein badlo, hal karo, aur shartein check karo.

blocks.title: Example 17
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\log_x(x^2 - 3x + 2) = 2\).
Maloom karna: real solutions \(x\).
Tareeqa: yahan unknown \(x\) base mein bhi hai. Is liye base aur argument dono ki shartein likhenge, exponential shakal mein badlenge, hal karenge, aur aakhir mein shartein check karenge.

Domain ki shartein
Base condition: \(x > 0,\ x \ne 1\)
Argument condition: \(x^2 - 3x + 2 > 0\)
Kyun: logarithm ka base positive aur 1 se mukhtalif hona chahiye (base 1 ki har power 1 hi hoti hai), aur argument positive hona chahiye.

Exponential shakal
\[x^2 = x^2 - 3x + 2\]
Kyun: \(\log_x u = 2 \iff u = x^2\). Yani base ki power 2 argument ke barabar hai.

Hal karein
\[3x - 2 = 0\]
\[x = \dfrac{2}{3}\]
Kyun: dono taraf \(x^2\) cancel ho gaya aur seedhi linear equation bachi.

Domain check karein
Base: \(x = \frac{2}{3} > 0\) aur \(x \ne 1\).
Argument:
\[\left(\tfrac{2}{3}\right)^2 - 3\left(\tfrac{2}{3}\right) + 2\]
\[= \tfrac{4}{9} - 2 + 2 = \tfrac{4}{9} > 0\]
Kyun: jo value kisi bhi shart ko toray, woh rad hoti; \(\frac{2}{3}\) dono shartein poori karti hai. Is liye \(x = \frac{2}{3}\) di gayi equation ka hal hai.

Tasdeeq:
\[\left(\tfrac{2}{3}\right)^2 = \tfrac{4}{9}\]
is liye \(\log_{\frac{2}{3}}\frac{4}{9} = 2\) \(\checkmark\)

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
(Yeh hamari practice hai, kitab ka sawal nahi.) \(\log_2(x + 1) + \log_2(x - 1) = 3\) hal karein.
Domain: \(x + 1 > 0\) aur \(x - 1 > 0\), yani \(x > 1\).
Product law: \(\log_2[(x + 1)(x - 1)] = 3\), yani \(x^2 - 1 = 2^3 = 8\).
Is liye \(x^2 = 9\), \(x = 3\) ya \(x = -3\). Domain sirf \(x = 3\) ko qabool karta hai.
Tasdeeq: \(\log_2 4 + \log_2 2 = 2 + 1 = 3\) \(\checkmark\)
Examples of Exponential and Logarithmic Inequations

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Inequality (nabarabri) bhi equation ki tarah hi hal hoti hai, bas ek sawal zyada poochna parta hai: jab hum exponential ya logarithm hatate hain to function barh raha hai (increasing) ya ghat raha hai (decreasing)? Base 1 se bara ho to nishan wohi rehta hai; base 0 aur 1 ke darmiyan ho to nishan ulat jata hai. Isay aise samjhein: seedhi seerhi par upar jane wala zyada unchai par hota hai, lekin ulti seerhi par aage jane wala neeche aa jata hai. Aakhri jawab hamesha (algebra wali inequality ka hal) \(\cap\) (domain) hota hai.

blocks.caption: Hamara khulasa: base hatane par inequality ka nishan kya hota hai
rows: \(a^x\) aur \(\log_a x\) strictly increasing (barhte hue) hain
\(a^x\) aur \(\log_a x\) strictly decreasing (ghatte hue) hain
Inequality ka nishan wohi rehta hai
Inequality ka nishan ulat jata hai

blocks.title: Example 19
steps:
Diya gaya: \(2^{x+1} > 5^x\).
Maloom karna: woh tamam real \(x\) jo inequality poori karein.
Tareeqa: positive number \(2^x\) se divide kar ke ek hi power \(\left(\frac{5}{2}\right)^x\) banayenge, phir base 10 ka logarithm lenge (increasing, is liye nishan wohi), power law lagayenge, aur aakhir mein positive number \(\log\frac{5}{2}\) se divide karenge.

Domain
\(2^{x+1}\) aur \(5^x\) dono har real number ke liye maujood hain.
Kyun: positive base wali exponential har power ke liye value deti hai.

Power ko torein
\[2 \cdot 2^x > 5^x\]
Kyun: \(2^{x+1} = 2^1 \cdot 2^x\).

\(2^x\) se divide karein
\[2 > \dfrac{5^x}{2^x}\]
\[2 > \left(\dfrac{5}{2}\right)^x\]
Kyun: \(2^x > 0\) har real number ke liye, aur positive se divide karne par nishan nahi badalta. Saath hi \(\frac{a^x}{b^x} = \left(\frac{a}{b}\right)^x\).

Base 10 ka logarithm lein
\[\log 2 > \log\left(\dfrac{5}{2}\right)^x\]
Kyun: base 10 wala logarithmic function strictly increasing hai: bare number ka log bhi bara. Is liye nishan wohi raha.

Power law
\[\log 2 > x\log\left(\dfrac{5}{2}\right)\]
Kyun: \(\log a^k = k\log a\); \(x\) power se neeche aa gaya.

\(\log\frac{5}{2}\) se divide karein
Kyunke \(\frac{5}{2} > 1\), is liye \(\log\left(\frac{5}{2}\right) > 0\):
\[x < \dfrac{\log 2}{\log\left(\frac{5}{2}\right)}\]
\[= \log_{\frac{5}{2}}(2) \approx 0.7565\]
Kyun: positive number se divide karne par nishan wohi rehta hai; change of base formula fraction ko ek logarithm bana deta hai.
Dhyan dein: \(\log\frac{5}{2}\) is liye positive hai ke \(\frac{5}{2}\) number 1 se bara hai; sirf positive hona kaafi nahi hota.

Tasdeeq:
\(x = 0\): \(2^1 = 2 > 5^0 = 1\) \(\checkmark\)
\(x = 1\): \(2^2 = 4 > 5^1 = 5\) ghalat hai, aur waqai \(1 > 0.7565\) jawab se bahar hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab yahan wajah yeh likhti hai: \(\frac{5}{2} > 0\), is liye \(\log\frac{5}{2} > 0\). Yeh wajah ghalat hai, kyunke sirf positive hona kaafi nahi: \(\frac{1}{2} > 0\) hai lekin \(\log\frac{1}{2} < 0\). Sahi wajah: \(\frac{5}{2} > 1\), is liye \(\log\left(\frac{5}{2}\right) > 0\). Aakhri jawab par koi asar nahi parta.

Agli misaal mein dono taraf base 10 ke logarithms hain. Yahan domain ek interval (faasla) ki shakal mein aata hai, is liye number line zehan mein rakhiye: pehle domain ka hissa number line par mark karein, phir algebra se jo hissa mile usay bhi mark karein, aur jahan dono milte hon wohi jawab hai. Kinaron (end points) par khaas dhyan dein: kaunsa kinara band bracket \([\ \ ]\) mein jayega aur kaunsa khula \(]\ \ [\) rahega.

blocks.title: Example 20
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\log(2x - 1) \ge \log(5 - 3x)\).
Maloom karna: woh tamam real \(x\) jo inequality poori karein.
Tareeqa: domain, phir logarithm hatayenge (base 10 increasing hai, is liye nishan wohi), linear inequality hal karenge, aur domain se intersection lenge.

Domain
\[2x - 1 > 0 \Rightarrow x > \tfrac{1}{2}\]
\[5 - 3x > 0 \Rightarrow x < \tfrac{5}{3}\]
\[\tfrac{1}{2} < x < \tfrac{5}{3}\]
Kyun: dono logarithms ke arguments positive hone chahiyen, is liye dono shartein ek saath lagti hain.

Logarithm hatayein
\[2x - 1 \ge 5 - 3x\]
Kyun: base 10 wala logarithmic function strictly increasing hai, is liye nishan wohi rehta hai.

Inequality hal karein
\[2x + 3x \ge 5 + 1\]
\[5x \ge 6\]
\[x \ge \tfrac{6}{5}\]
Kyun: \(x\) wali terms ek taraf, numbers doosri taraf; phir positive 5 se divide (nishan wohi).

Domain se milayein
\[\tfrac{6}{5} \le x < \tfrac{5}{3}\]
Kyun: \(\frac{6}{5} = 1.2\) domain \(]\frac{1}{2}, \frac{5}{3}[\) ke andar hai. \(\frac{5}{3}\) wala kinara khula rehta hai, kyunke wahan \(\log(5 - 3x) = \log 0\) maujood nahi.

Tasdeeq:
\(x = 1.5\): \(\log 2 \ge \log 0.5\) \(\checkmark\)
\(x = 1\): \(\log 1 = 0 \ge \log 2\) ghalat, jaisa hona chahiye tha (\(1 < 1.2\)).

blocks.text: Ab is sabaq ki sab se mazedar misaal. Is mein teen cheezein ek saath aati hain: quadratic ka domain, base 1 se chhota hone ki wajah se ulta nishan, aur aakhir mein do hisson wala jawab. Aaram se, qadam ba qadam chalenge. Agar aap is misaal ko khud se dobara hal kar lein to Exercise 1.4 ka Question 2 aap ke liye aasan ho jayega.

blocks.title: Example 21
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\log_{\frac{7}{9}}(x^2 - 3x + 2) \ge \log_{\frac{7}{9}}(2x - 1)\).
Maloom karna: woh tamam real \(x\) jo inequality poori karein.
Tareeqa: dono logarithms ka domain; base \(\frac{7}{9}\) 0 aur 1 ke darmiyan hai, is liye function decreasing hai aur log hatate waqt nishan ulat jayega; phir quadratic inequality hal kar ke domain se intersection.

Pehle logarithm ka domain
\[x^2 - 3x + 2 > 0\]
\[(x - 1)(x - 2) > 0\]
\[x < 1 \text{ or } x > 2\]
Kyun: product positive tab hota hai jab dono factors negative hon (\(x < 1\) aur \(x < 2\), yani \(x < 1\)) ya dono positive hon (\(x > 1\) aur \(x > 2\), yani \(x > 2\)).

Doosre logarithm ka domain
\[2x - 1 > 0 \Rightarrow x > \tfrac{1}{2}\]

Mila hua domain
\[]\tfrac{1}{2}, 1[ \cup ]2, \infty[\]
Kyun: dono shartein ek saath: \(x < 1\) ya \(x > 2\) mein se sirf woh hissa jahan \(x > \frac{1}{2}\) bhi ho.

Logarithm hatayein (nishan ulta)
\[x^2 - 3x + 2 \le 2x - 1\]
\[x^2 - 5x + 3 \le 0\]
Kyun: \(0 < \frac{7}{9} < 1\), is liye \(\log_{\frac{7}{9}}\) strictly decreasing hai: bara logarithm chhote argument ka hota hai. Is liye \(\ge\) badal kar \(\le\) ho gaya.
Dhyan dein: yahan nishan na ulatna is sawal ki sab se aam ghalti hai.

\(x^2 - 5x + 3 = 0\) hal karein
\[x = \dfrac{5 \pm \sqrt{25 - 12}}{2}\]
\[= \dfrac{5 \pm \sqrt{13}}{2}\]
Kyun: quadratic formula, \(a = 1,\ b = -5,\ c = 3\).

\(x^2 - 5x + 3 \le 0\) kahan hai?
\[\dfrac{5 - \sqrt{13}}{2} \le x \le \dfrac{5 + \sqrt{13}}{2}\]
Kyun: doosra imkaan, yani \(x \le \frac{5 - \sqrt{13}}{2}\) aur \(x \ge \frac{5 + \sqrt{13}}{2}\) ek saath, na-mumkin hai. Is liye \(x\) dono roots ke darmiyan hai (lagbhag \(0.697 \le x \le 4.303\)).

Domain se milayein
\[x \in [\tfrac{5 - \sqrt{13}}{2}, 1[\]
\[\text{or } x \in ]2, \tfrac{5 + \sqrt{13}}{2}]\]
Kyun: \(\frac{5 - \sqrt{13}}{2} \approx 0.697\) number \(\frac{1}{2}\) se bara hai, is liye pehla hissa wahin se shuru hota hai; 1 aur 2 domain ki wajah se bahar hain; dono kinare \(\frac{5 \pm \sqrt{13}}{2}\) shamil hain kyunke barabari ki ijazat hai aur wahan dono arguments positive hain.

Tasdeeq:
\(x = 3\): \(x^2 - 3x + 2 = 2\) aur \(2x - 1 = 5\). Kyunke \(2 < 5\) aur base 1 se chhota hai, \(\log_{\frac{7}{9}} 2 > \log_{\frac{7}{9}} 5\) \(\checkmark\)

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Agar \(\log_{\frac{1}{2}} u > \log_{\frac{1}{2}} v\) ho (aur \(u, v > 0\)), to \(u\) aur \(v\) mein kaunsa bara hai? (Jawab: base \(\frac{1}{2}\) 1 se chhota hai, function decreasing hai, is liye \(u < v\).)

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
(Yeh hamari practice hai, kitab ka sawal nahi.) \(\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^x > \frac{1}{8}\) hal karein.
\(\frac{1}{8} = \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^3\), is liye \(\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^x > \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^3\).
Base \(\frac{1}{2}\) 0 aur 1 ke darmiyan hai, is liye nishan ulat jayega: \(x < 3\).
Tasdeeq: \(x = 0\) par \(1 > \frac{1}{8}\) \(\checkmark\); \(x = 4\) par \(\frac{1}{16} > \frac{1}{8}\) ghalat. Solution set: \(]-\infty, 3[\).

Aakhir mein poore sabaq ko ek jumle mein samet lete hain: pehle domain, phir sahi auzaar (ek jaisa base, logarithm lena, ya laws), phir algebra, aur aakhir mein domain se milaan aur tasdeeq. Inequality mein bas itna yaad rakhiye ke base hatate waqt function ka mizaaj (increasing ya decreasing) dekhna hai. Yahi tarteeb Exercise 1.4 ke har sawal mein kaam aayegi.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Hamesha pehle domain: har logarithm ka argument positive (aur base positive, 1 ke ilawa).
2. Dono taraf ek hi base ho to powers ya arguments barabar rakh dein (one-to-one property).
3. Base alag alag hon to dono taraf logarithm lein aur power law lagayein.
4. Kai logarithms hon to product ya quotient law se ek banayein, phir exponential shakal mein badlein.
5. Inequality mein: base 1 se bara to nishan wohi; base 0 aur 1 ke darmiyan to nishan ulta.
6. Aakhri jawab = (algebra wala hal) \(\cap\) (domain); ek value andar aur ek bahar se check karein.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Domain bhool jana: \(\log x + \log(x - 3) = 1\) mein \(x = -2\) ko rad karna zaroori hai, warna jawab ghalat.
2. Base 0 aur 1 ke darmiyan ho phir bhi nishan wohi rakhna (Example 21 dekhiye).
3. Kisi logarithm se divide karna aur us ka sign na dekhna: \(0 < a < 1\) ho to \(\log a < 0\), aur phir nishan ulat jata hai.
4. Aisa kinara shamil kar lena jahan logarithm \(\log 0\) ban jaye (Example 20 mein \(x = \frac{5}{3}\) shamil nahi).
5. \(\log(m + n) = \log m + \log n\) likhna: sahi product law \(\log(mn) = \log m + \log n\) hai.
